name: Hungary — Hungarian parties
intro: compare it with Hungarian political parties
inclusion_note: The test includes the main national parties of Hungary: those represented in the parliament (Országgyűlés) and those with a significant national following. Positions are the team's estimates and are open to review.
hemicycle_note: Seats in the parliament (Országgyűlés) after the 2022 election, arranged left to right. Approximate. 199 members. A more recent election is not yet reflected in these seats; the party list includes parties that are strong in current polls. Parties shown without seats are included because they poll strongly.

DK.name: Demokratikus Koalíció
DK.priorities: Rule of law, Deeper European integration, Welfare state
DK.description: Democratic Coalition, the centre-left party founded by former prime minister Ferenc Gyurcsány and for years the largest opposition party.

Momentum.name: Momentum Mozgalom
Momentum.priorities: Rule of law, Education, Deeper European integration
Momentum.description: Liberal, pro-European party of a younger generation.

MKKP.name: Magyar Kétfarkú Kutya Párt
MKKP.priorities: Transparency and digital rights, Democratic reform
MKKP.description: Hungarian Two-Tailed Dog Party, a satirical party that mocks the political system and does practical local projects.

Volt.name: Volt Magyarország
Volt.priorities: Deeper European integration, Climate action, Digital innovation, Democratic reform
Volt.description: National chapter of Volt Europa, the first pan-European party. All chapters share one programme: a federal and more democratic EU, evidence-based policy, a market economy with a strong welfare state, and the digital and climate transitions. Volt has the same positions in every country in this test.

Tisza.name: Tisztelet és Szabadság Párt (Tisza)
Tisza.priorities: Fighting corruption, Rule of law, Public healthcare, Deeper European integration
Tisza.description: Respect and Freedom Party of Péter Magyar, a former Fidesz insider; it became the main challenger to Viktor Orbán ahead of the 2026 election, campaigning against corruption and for EU funds.

Fidesz–KDNP.name: Fidesz–KDNP
Fidesz–KDNP.ideologies: National conservatism, Right-wing populism, Soft Euroscepticism, Sovereignism
Fidesz–KDNP.priorities: National sovereignty, Traditional family values, Reducing immigration, Diplomacy with Russia, no arms deliveries
Fidesz–KDNP.description: Viktor Orbán's national-conservative alliance, in power since 2010; it describes Hungary as an 'illiberal democracy', clashes with the EU over the rule of law and opposes military aid to Ukraine.

Mi Hazánk.name: Mi Hazánk Mozgalom
Mi Hazánk.priorities: National identity, National sovereignty, Reducing immigration
Mi Hazánk.description: Our Homeland Movement, a far-right party to the right of Fidesz.
